items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: You know that famous recording ... of George W. Thomas’s “The Rocks” ... Do you know that record?

ctx.x: Yeah because, “Oh that’s a Claude Hopkins lick,” but as you already stated, these licks man are traded all over.

Well a lot of jazz discography consists of well-meaning guesswork I think. But I don’t think we’re any better off for it. Because sometimes if you have information like that that you think is accurate then it’s going to discourage you from trying to look for what might actually be the case. You know that famous recording — not famous — famous to record collectors, of George W. Thomas’s “The Rocks” by a young pianist represented as Clay Custer, a 1923 recording? Do you know that record? Well it’s represented as…
Oh yes, and like the way Bessie Smith passed away and so forth.
